page.layout: One column of running text on a single printed page. Page number top left. Running head top right, set in decorative type. Catchword at the lower right. Quotation marks at the left edge of the column.

main_text.p: cauedum peritus effet. Nam hac definitione is folus conti-netur, qui de iure jam certo, & vel scripto, vel moribus constituto respondet. id quod Pragmaticorum munus fuisse, superius dicebamus: qui quantum à Iurisconsultis differant, ex his Quintiliani verbis in lib. XII cap. iii, facile in tellectu est: ubi quę Iurisconsultorum responsis explicantur, aut in verborũ interpretatione posita esse scribit, aut in recti prauiqué discrimine: cùm alij se ad album ac rubricas transferant, & formula-rij, vel (ut Cicero ait) legulei quidam efficiantur. page.notes: The running head is a decorative row of blocks and could not be read; it is marked illegible. The "»" marks at the start of each line are quotation markers at the column edge, not printed text, so they are left out. The phrase "tellectu" after "in" is set with a ligature I could not resolve with certainty; the reading "intellectu" is likely, but the word is given as "telleCtu" in the printed form and should be checked. Long s is shown as f in the scan ("fuisse", "conti-netur") and is normalised to s. The hyphenated line ends "conti-" and "formula-" are kept with their printed hyphens. The final "il-" stands below the last full line and is treated as the catchword.
